summary: Redefines the DNS Authenticated Data (AD) bit. Based on implementation experience, the original meaning from RFC 2535 turned out to be not useful. It becomes set only when all answers, or the records proving no answers exist, were cryptographically verified or meet the server's local security policy. It has been replaced by RFCs 4033, 4034 and 4035.

eli5.summary: A checkmark on a DNS answer says it was checked. This made the checkmark mean something clearer and safer. Newer DNSSEC documents, RFCs 4033 to 4035, have since replaced it.
